text_blocks.snippet: A professional roof inspection in Utah typically costs [Highlight start] $100 to $400 [Highlight end] for a paid or formal inspection, though many local roofing contractors offer free inspections when you are looking for a repair or replacement estimate.

list.snippet: Free: Basic visual inspections and estimates from roofing contractors evaluating potential repairs, storm damage, or roof replacement.
$75–$150: Written summary reports from a roofer or inspector.
$150–$400: Independent third-party or formal documented inspections—often used for real estate transactions, insurance claims, or detailed photo reports.
Up to $500–$600: Specialized methods (such as infrared imaging) or comprehensive hard-copy/third-party reports for steep, large, or complex roofs.

text_blocks.snippet: Full Stack Roofing outlines typical pricing tiers for basic, written, and formal Utah roof inspections, while A&A Roofing details what a documented Utah inspection covers, including snow-load/ice dam risks, hail, and UV wear. If you need broader context on project pricing, Rooval Roofing provides a 2026 guide to Utah roof replacement costs.

list.snippet: Purpose of the inspection: Contractor sales/repair estimates are often free, whereas neutral third-party reports for buying/selling a home or insurance disputes usually carry a fee. On , opinions are mixed—some note inspections starting around $500 with a hard-copy report, while others point out many roofers provide free multi-point inspections and estimates.
Roof size, pitch, and access: Steep slopes, multi-story homes, or snow/ice coverage require extra time or specialized equipment .
Documentation depth: Photo logs, attic/ventilation checks, and formal written reports cost more than a quick walk-around.

text_blocks.snippet: Are you looking for a free repair/replacement estimate, or do you need an independent inspection for a home purchase, sale, or insurance claim? Sharing your and roof type can also help narrow down what to expect.
